thread:
jia: Heads-up — we just hit a regional GPU surge in us-central1, nodepool-gpu-preemptible saturated, CA backing off with too many pending pods.
sam: saw that. pods are piling in the priority queue, autoscaler log shows ScaleUp blocked: insufficient quota in zone-a.
oliver: is this the cross-zone spillover we talked about? any chance we can route requests to us-west1 spare capacity?
marta: we can, but routing will need a model-variant or smaller GPU instance. Some models aren't compatible with the quantized variant.
jia: infra-bot posted the error earlier: `ClusterAutoscaler: ScaleUp: ignored because node group node-pool-gpu-1 has no available capacity in zone-a`
infra-bot: @here detected capacity constraint in zone-a: free GPUs=0, inflight requests=42, recommend: trigger cross-cluster allocation or progressive downgrade.
sam: proposal: add a temporary nodepool-gpu-burst in us-central1-b with mixed-preemptible+on-demand mix and set max surge to 6, then drain low-priority pods to it. Quick to create via terraform.
oliver: +1 but careful with scheduling — need proper taints/tolerations and nodeSelector for gpu.family==a100. Otherwise pods will land on incompatible hw.
marta: i'll draft toleration and label plan, and a fallback routing rule in our model router. snippet: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Node nodeSelector: gpu.family: a100 tolerations: - key: "gpu-burst" operator: "Exists" effect: "NoSchedule" ```
jia: also modify cluster-autoscaler flags: `--max-total-unready-percentage=50` and `--expendable-pods-priority-cutoff=2000` to allow evicting low-priority batch when scale is stuck.
sam: watch out — changing expendable cutoff can evict some eval jobs. We should only do that for the burst pool via node affinity, not cluster-wide.
oliver: alternative: enable cross-cluster allocation policy: `routePolicy: prefer-region` with weight to us-west1 when us-central1 > 90% util. That avoids evictions.
marta: routing change needs console UI + API gating for Dedicated customers. can we make it automatic for internal test clusters first?
jia: yes, test cluster first. Also add a short TTL for cross-cluster failover (10m) to avoid long tail latency.
sam: cost note: routing to us-west1 on-demand will roughly double per-token infra cost for heavy models. We need finance signoff if we keep this longer than 30m.\ioliver: typo: sam -> oliver.\oliver: finance pinged: @finance we can absorb up to ~$2k for emergency bursts monthly, anything beyond needs approval.
infra-bot: action created: #ticket-4821 - create nodepool-gpu-burst, apply taints, add CA policy, and add routing TTL=10m. assigned to marta.
marta: starting terraform plan now. will post the plan in this thread.
sam: once up, we should test a canary traffic shift: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 5m windows and monitor p95 latency, cost, and error rates.
jia: agreed. if p95 jumps >200ms or error rate >1% we rollback to local queue and trigger quota backpressure.
marta: terraform plan: `resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_burst" { name = "gpu-burst" initial_node_count = 2 autoscaling { min_node_count = 0 max_node_count = 6 } node_config { machine_type = "n2-standard-16" accelerators { type = "nvidia-tesla-a100" count = 1 } taint { key = "gpu-burst" value = "true" effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" } labels = { gpu.family = "a100" } } }`
oliver: make sure rollout uses `podTopologySpread` to avoid packing all pods on a single host in the burst pool.
sam: also enable KV caching policy to reduce token costs during the burst, small optimization but helps.
jia: let's run through checklist: 1) create nodepool (marta) 2) add CA flags on test cluster (sam) 3) routing TTL + policy (oliver) 4) canary traffic plan + metrics (jia) 5) finance watch (finance)
marta: ok aiming to apply in 12m, will update.
infra-bot: update: nodepool creation started (ticket #4821).
